newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Soccer-Algeria must wait on result in Bouake.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Algeria must wait on result in Bouake.

text.p: Former African champions Algeria and Egypt head a list of rated teams who may miss out on next year's African Nations' Cup finals if they do not win in this weekend's final round of qualifying matches.
Both north African countries, who have won four African titles between them, must also rely on their closest rivals being beaten if they are to line up in the 16-team tournament next February.
With nine places already filled, the identity of the remaining seven will be known after the weekend's 11 qualifying matches.

Algeria, in particular, face a repeat of their elimination from the World Cup finals in Spain 15 years ago when a contrived result in another group match between Austria and West Germany cost them progress into the knockout phase of the competition -- and the distinction of becoming the first African country to go past the group matches in the World Cup finals.
Algeria must beat Benin in Algiers on Sunday and then hope there is a result in the other group match between Ivory Coast and Mali in Bouake at the same time to qualify.
There will be a sense of deja vu for the north Africans as they await the result from Bouake, where a draw will be enough for both the Ivorians and their Malian neighbours to qualify.

Their World Cup elimination 15 years ago, when the Germans beat Austria 1-0 in Gijons and both teams qualified for the second round, still rankles the Algerians and there will be more than just a critical eye if the Ivorians and Mali show as little enhusiasm for a result as the Austrians and Germans did in Spain more than a decade ago.
Egypt, who have won the Nations Cup three times, must also rely on the result of their other group match to go through.
They trail second-placed Senegal by three points in group three, but have the advantage of an easy home match against Ethiopia while Senegal are away at Morocco on Sunday.

The odds would normally be in Egypt's favour as their last home match against Ethiopia saw them score six goals without reply and Senegal would ordinarily not be given much chance of avoiding defeat in Morocco.

But Morocco have already qualified for the finals in top place in group three, as well as making the World Cup finals in France next year, and could treat Sunday's match as nothing more than a training exercise and an opportunity to blood fringe players. That would suddenly open the door for the draw that Senegal need to qualify and leave Egypt, who have frosty football relationships with their north African rivals, out in the cold.
Malawi, Namibia and Zimbabwe also just need one point to secure qualification but all play away against the teams seeking to displace them.
Angola host Zimbabwe in group one in Luanda on Sunday while Namibia are at Gabon in Libreville the same day.
Malawi travel to Mozambique in group seven on Saturday, seeking to qualify for the finals for only the second time.
Home wins in all three of those matches would see Angola, Gabon and Mozambique return for a second successive appearance at the finals.

The newly-named Democratic Republic of Congo, who have not won in four matches since changing from Zaire, renaming their team 'Simba' instead of the Leopards and wearing all-blue, can still go through if they beat Togo at home in Kinshasa in group sixon Sunday.
But a draw would allow the possible winner of the match between Liberia and Tanzania in Monrovia to sneak through in second place behind the Togolese.
Hosts Burkina Faso and holders South Africa qualified for the finals automatically while Cameroon, Ghana, Morocco, Togo and Zambia secured their places earlier this month.

Sierra Leone's withdrawal from their final two matches in group four means Guinea and Tunisia also qualified, although this will only be properly ratified when the Confederation of African Football's executive committee meets in Cairo nxt month.
